How am I sure that human-like aliens do count in the decimal system?

Aleksander Kantak · 13 October 2022

Our thinking about numbers is so biased that thinking in a different way is too abstract for most of us. If you don’t feel like thinking abstract right now, don’t read further. I will try to abstract our decimal systems as often as I can.

Let’s assume, that we calculate in decimal numbers (base-ten positional numeral system) because we have two hands, five fingers each, so ten fingers.

Oh, I can’t say ten, because it is already biased with our ten-based system (inception, huh?). In the same way, I can’t use “higher” base numbers, like hexadecimal because of the “decimal” in them.

Let me explain in detail how that base-ten positional numeral system works. Let’s count sheep. I will start with 0. None of the fingers extended. I saw one sheep, and I extended my finger, so now I have 1. I add another one and I get 2. Now, let’s add 1 more. Now I get 3. And then 4, and 5, and 6, then 7, and 8. With another one added I get 9. I hope that was the last one because I almost got out of my fingers.

And now we have the fun part. You see another one, extend the last finger. If I want to add one more to my last number, I get 10.

Wait, what? One and zero? Why do we have digits only up to 9?

Adding one more finger to my already used nine fingers gives us the completed set. The pack of fingers. 5 + 5. You can’t count more on your fingers.

I will call my friend, we would count together, he would be my first exponent. That means he would count my completed packs of fingers. I “give” him my one completed pack, so now he has one finger extended, and I fold all my fingers.

So he has one finger extended and I have none.

He has 1 extended and I have 0.

So, together, we have 1 and 0.

In short 10.

So what was with those aliens?

What if on another planet aliens called Eart, the highest evolution form residents would have two hands with only 4 fingers on each hand? And that creature would have to count the same sheep they bought from Earth that we counted previously.

No worries, people from Earth and Eart speak the same English language and both use the decimal systems, so we should be cool, right?

Let’s count. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7. Almost out of the fingers. Oh, another one, so now I have 10.

Wait, what?

They do use the decimal system, so why after 7 they got 10 instead of 8?

Because it is the completed pack of fingers for them. They don’t have digits 8 and 9 because they don’t need them. Their 10 is 4+4, the sum of both hands' fingers. We, creatures from Earth, would call it the octal numeral system or base-8 number system.

But if we would talk with characters from EARTHEAR where primates have 8 fingers on each hand, “our decimal” would be a base-A number system for them. Because in “our hexadecimal” i.e. their decimal, where the pack of fingers is 8+8, there is a “digit” for our pack of fingers, i.e. 5+5, and it is “digit A”. They count 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, A, B, C, D, E, F, 10.

By the way, our nerds do count in 8+8 too. We use that to talk with the computers. Maybe computers come from Earthear planet…

So why am I claiming, that all aliens use the decimal system since I’ve described something opposite? The answer is in the definition of the “decimal” word. The name decimal means only that you use 1 and 0 as a number equal to the full pack of the fingers. But it does not say how much exactly is it…
